scientificObservations: Three separated evidence cards show a lateral lower-jaw fragment, an approximately bilaterally symmetric pelvis schematic with iliac wings and sacral center, and a lateral skull. They are generic fossil evidence types, not three named taxa or anatomically exact museum reconstructions.

The blue/red/green card identity survives into the hypothesis branch. The older-to-younger arrow and the large explicit Abfolge ≠ Abstammung statement distinguish chronology from a proven ancestor sequence. The small dotted branching hypothesis is marked with question marks; it does not assert that A directly gave rise to B and C.

The jaw and skull retain plausible schematic articulation and teeth, and the pelvic schematic has no concrete scientifically misleading required detail. There is no walking-progress parade, race hierarchy, or numerical age falsely presented as fossil evidence.

Dating intervals, uncertain overlap and evidential trait interpretation remain in the actual goal/cases. This overview illustration introduces their reasoning and is not a standalone dated fossil dataset or P/source proof.

scientificObservations: Two scene panels show an adult and learner putting mulch on soil, then that learner sharing garden/water practice with another learner. The arrow Lernen, repeated leaf/water bubbles and Weitergeben/Verändern sign communicate socially transmitted and changeable practices.

A separated bottom DNA schematic is labeled Vererbung. No arrow transfers DNA into the learnt garden method or claims that acquired knowledge modifies inherited genes. This is a visual contrast between learning/cultural transmission and biological inheritance.

The two blue DNA backbone curves maintain plausible alternating front/back crossings and continuous curve direction through the hidden intersections. Colored connectors meet the schematic ladder; no disconnected concealed-helix section is visible.

A low-water cylinder, sun and dry soil/plants form a separate limitation inset beside the rainwater tank. Beneficial garden practice is therefore not presented as limitless success under all environmental conditions. No quantitative performance or causal learner experiment is asserted.

The gardening scene communicates a culturally passed-on practice affecting present people and environment. Detailed evidence weighing, confounders and changed-world tests remain in the goal/cases; the drawing is an orientation illustration, not their full assessment proof.
rows.actorAndPerspective: The adult/learners look toward their work or one another. Hands, mulch, watering-can spout and water flow face the intended activity. The background sign and diagram labels are external explanatory labels; no actor is depicted writing or reading a backwards notebook.
rows.360Observation: Both repeated learner scenes, learning arrow, separate DNA/Vererbung and low-water/dry-soil inset remain recognizable. The upper-right Weitergeben/Verändern sign is comparatively small, but is supplementary to the visible peer-teaching scene and readable main Lernen label; no required new tiny explanatory paragraph is present.
